page: Microsoft Azure D32ds_v5 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DDSv5 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8370C processor operating at 2.8 GHz. The architecture is x86_64, supported by 128.0 GB of system memory, which equates to 4.0 GB per core. The CPU includes an L3 cache of 48 MB and supports instruction sets such as AVX-512 Foundation, AVX-512 Vector Neural Network Instructions (VNNI), and AES cryptography.

This instance is bundled with 1229 GB of local SSD storage and is Premium Storage capable, allowing integration with high-performance external disks. It does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or GPU hardware.

Benchmark data places the D32ds_v5 in the average performance tier across most compute, memory, and compression tests. It achieved a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 31064.56 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14148.0. In memory tests, it recorded a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 1679.52 GB/sec and a large block uncached write bandwidth of 69.03 GB/sec. For language model workloads, the instance demonstrates a clear performance tradeoff: while text generation with a small 135M model is strong at 287.54 tokens/sec, performance drops to a weak 6.67 tokens/sec for 70B model prompt processing and a poor 2.29 tokens/sec for 70B text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D32ds_v5 offers a balanced resource density of compute, memory, and local SSD storage, making it suitable for workloads that require moderate local scratch space without the premium cost of memory-optimized or GPU-accelerated hardware. Appropriate workloads include database operations, static web serving, software compilation, and small-to-medium scale machine learning inference.
